questions.q: Where do Scheduled Job records live in ServiceNow?
options: The sysauto_script table
The sys_properties table
The syslog table
The sys_update_set table
questions.explain: Scheduled Jobs are stored as records in the sysauto_script table.

questions.q: What triggers a Scheduled Job to run, in contrast to what triggers a Business Rule?
options: A specific record being inserted or updated, exactly like a Business Rule
A user manually clicking a button on the job record
A defined schedule — a time, repeat interval, or recurring pattern — regardless of any record activity
A field changing value on any table in the instance
questions.explain: A Scheduled Job runs on a timer configured in its Run field; it doesn't need any record to change at all.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, named example of a housekeeping-style scheduled job discussed in this lesson?
options: A job that purges old rows out of the system log so syslog doesn't grow without bound
A job that creates new user accounts automatically
A job that enforces table-level ACLs
A job that renders the Service Catalog UI
questions.explain: Cleanup/housekeeping jobs, including ones that trim old log data, are a real category of out-of-box scheduled job.

questions.q: What field on a Scheduled Job record tells you exactly when it's due to run next?
options: Description
Next action
Active
Condition
questions.explain: Next action shows the exact time the job is scheduled to fire next — the first place to check if a job seems to be missing runs.

questions.q: Which task is a Scheduled Job's kind of work, per this lesson's own example?
options: Setting the assignment group the moment a specific new Incident is created
Finding all SLAs due to breach in the next hour, with nobody having edited any record to trigger it
Validating one field on a single form before save
Displaying a related list on a record's form
questions.explain: A Scheduled Job sweeps across records on a timer, independent of any single record event — exactly the SLA-breach-sweep example.
